facts.topic: Q1 class hierarchy
facts.detail: Expression (ABC, __slots__=('_key','_shape')) has exactly 4 concrete subclasses used by the grammar: Feature(field:str), Constant(value:float), _OpNode (abstract, holds spec/operands/window) with its 4 leaf subclasses Unary/Binary/Rolling/PairRolling (category-specific arity checks only), and GeneralCall (arbitrary arity, literal args, tuple-of-tensor args, 'exempt' operand positions). GeneralCall is never produced by make_node/the search grammar -- only the parser builds it, for research/legacy expressions reaching outside the 4-category grammar.
facts.refs: expression.py:48-107 (Expression base), 110-123 (Feature), 126-141 (Constant), 199-266 (_OpNode/Unary/Binary/Rolling/PairRolling), 285-322 (GeneralCall.__init__)

facts.topic: Q1 shape system
facts.detail: Shape is a frozen dataclass with exactly 2 independent booleans (collapsed, degenerate) plus an optional int width; 'daily' is NOT a third independent axis -- it is a read-only property that returns `self.degenerate` verbatim. 3 named module constants cover the combinations actually used: FULL=(False,False,None) = genuine per-minute tensor; COLLAPSED=(True,True,1) = day_*/restores_m-target, one real minute column; WIDE_DEGENERATE=(False,True,None) = full minute width but every column identical (Constant, in_expand's own output). A 4th, unnamed combination (arbitrary literal width 1<w<full, degenerate True or False) is produced ad hoc by _passthrough/GeneralCall for literal-width slices (e.g. in_slice(x,10,229) -> width=220). collapsed=True with degenerate=False is never constructed anywhere in the current code -- an invariant that holds by convention, not by an assertion.
facts.refs: expression.py:28-41 (Shape, FULL, COLLAPSED, WIDE_DEGENERATE), 34-36 (`daily` aliases `degenerate`), 175-196 (_passthrough/_output_shape produce the ad hoc 4th combination), test_expression.py:8-21 (test_shape_typing exercises all 3 named shapes plus FULL on a bare Feature)

facts.topic: Q1 make_node shape checks
facts.detail: make_node dispatches by spec.category to Unary/Binary/Rolling/PairRolling; _OpNode.__init__ is the single place that (a) checks operand count against the category's expected arity, (b) checks window presence against spec.requires_window, (c) calls operand_ok(spec, operand, strict) on every operand and raises ShapeError(_why_not(...)) on the first failure. GeneralCall.__init__ duplicates a SEPARATE, non-identical check (arity is unchecked/-1, tuple args unpacked, 'exempt' positions skipped) -- any change meant to also affect research/legacy (GeneralCall) trees must be made in both places.
facts.refs: expression.py:199-216 (_OpNode.__init__), 269-279 (make_node), 302-322 (GeneralCall.__init__, separate check)

facts.topic: Q1 is_valid_root
facts.detail: is_valid_root(expr) is exactly 3 conditions ANDed: (1) expr.shape.degenerate (both COLLAPSED and WIDE_DEGENERATE roots qualify); (2) the ROOT node's OWN spec.non_root must be False (non_root = boolean_output or coarse_output, axes.py:112-114) -- this is a root-only check, it does NOT walk descendants, so a boolean op anywhere BELOW the root (e.g. pow_05(eq(a,b))) is NOT caught by is_valid_root at all; (3) `any(isinstance(n, Feature) for n in expr.nodes())` -- at least one Feature leaf anywhere in the tree (constant-only trees like sigmoid(5) are rejected).
facts.refs: expression.py:398-404; test_expression.py:8-25 (table incl. is_gt0(day_mean(Ret))->root=False, cs_rank(mul(day_mean(Close),2))->root=True), test_expression.py:43-45 (constant-only tree)

facts.topic: Q1 the real defense against 'laundered' booleans
facts.detail: Because is_valid_root only inspects the ROOT's own flag, the actual mechanism keeping boolean/trivial operators out of search trees ENTIRELY (not just as roots) is Registry.searchable(include_boolean=False), which filters them out of the operator VOCABULARY a generator may place anywhere in a tree. catalog.py's own docstring records a real incident: pow_05(eq(a,b)) reached rank 1 of a generation with spurious |IC| 0.58 before this filter existed. So 'declare an operator real-valued' (Q4) and is_valid_root (Q1) are two independent levers; fixing the OpSpec flag at registration time (as Partura's dataclasses.replace already does) automatically satisfies BOTH -- re-admits the op to searchable() AND lets it be a legal root -- with one change.
facts.refs: catalog.py:353-372 (Registry.searchable docstring + implementation), axes.py:112-114 (non_root)

facts.topic: Q1 key() construction
facts.detail: key() is lazily computed once and cached on the instance via object.__setattr__ (bypassing __slots__ immutability) into the base class's _key slot. Per-kind, type-tagged format: Feature -> 'F:{field}'; Constant -> 'C:{value!r}' (exact float repr, so 1.0 vs 1.0000001 differ); _OpNode -> 'O:{spec.name}({child.key(),...}){|wN}'; GeneralCall -> 'G:{spec.name}({rendered args})' where a literal renders as 'L:{a!r}', a tuple-of-exprs as '[e.key(),...]'. key() (not object identity) is the sole structural-equality/hash basis (__eq__/__hash__ both delegate to it) and is consumed well beyond expression.py: GP population dedup and ban-list lookups (mining/gp.py), the mutation/growth env (mining/env.py), seed/boosting dedup (mining/boosting.py, pipeline.py), and DAG common-subexpression identity (engine/dag.py).
facts.refs: expression.py:65-74 (key()/_make_key base), 116-117 (Feature), 132-133 (Constant), 226-229 (_OpNode), 335-342 (GeneralCall); test_expression.py:48-55; consumers: mining/gp.py:260,374,444,463,535,558,591,716-717,883; mining/env.py:144,204,239,275; mining/boosting.py:100-102; mining/generator.py:65,145,148; engine/dag.py:17,61; pipeline.py:107-108

facts.topic: Q2 constant recognition
facts.detail: A bare numeric literal becomes Constant iff `isinstance(node.value,(int,float)) and not isinstance(node.value,bool)` -- the explicit bool exclusion matters because Python's ast.Constant.value for True/False IS an int instance (bool subclasses int); without the guard, True/False would silently become Constant(1.0)/Constant(0.0). The same not-isinstance(x,bool) guard is repeated at every literal boundary: unary-minus constant folding, GeneralCall literal args, window_literal, and GeneralCall.literal_width.
facts.refs: parser.py:112 (convert), 189 and 193-195 (call(), GeneralCall literal args + negative-literal), 220-223 (window_literal); expression.py:330-332 (literal_width)

facts.topic: Q2 strict vs lenient operand rules
facts.detail: operand_ok(spec, operand, strict) has 2 strict-gated relaxations, both OFF by default (strict=True is the search grammar's rule): (a) restores_m (in_expand): strict requires operand.shape.collapsed exactly (width==1 AND degenerate); non-strict only requires operand.shape.degenerate (so a WIDE_DEGENERATE operand, e.g. mul(day_mean(Close),2), is accepted in in_expand only when non-strict). (b) needs_full_m (which covers BOTH in_*/day_* (face=='dt' and family in ('in','day')) AND nt_*): if the operand genuinely varies per minute (not degenerate) it is always fine; if degenerate, strict always rejects, non-strict accepts ONLY when the operator itself reduces_m (day_*) AND the operand is specifically collapsed (width==1) -- i.e. the non-strict carve-out exists for day_*-over-day_*, never for in_*/nt_* over a degenerate operand. needs_daily (nd face: cs_*/ts_*) has no strict/non-strict distinction at all: it only ever requires sh.degenerate. cross_* and elementwise ops are unrestricted in both modes (fall through to the final `return True`).
facts.refs: expression.py:144-172 (operand_ok, _why_not); axes.py:88-96 (needs_full_m, needs_daily); test_expression.py:28-40 (test_shape_errors, all under strict); test_general_call.py:47-49 (parse(...,strict=True) rejects, parse_legacy allows the day_*-over-width-1 case)

facts.topic: Q2 coerce_daily and allow_general
facts.detail: allow_general=False makes self.full=None, so any name outside the 4-category registry raises ParseError('unknown operator') instead of falling into GeneralCall -- the switch between 'search-grammar-only' and the 'research/legacy full surface'. coerce_daily=True sets self.daily_fields=True for the WHOLE parse iff the expression tree contains NO minute-level operator at all (checked once up front by uses_minute_operators, which looks only at face in ('dt','nt') after alias/arity resolution); when true, every bare field name resolves to its DAILY macro (Feature('Close') becomes day_last(Close) etc, via DAILY_OF_FIELD) instead of the raw minute Feature. If the tree DOES use a minute operator, bare fields stay minute-level, and coercion instead happens node-locally in .coerce()/.daily_of(): only when a raw-field subtree is fed directly as an operand of an ND-face (cs_*/ts_*) operator is it wrapped in its day_* macro; coercion recurses through 'shared'-face (elementwise) ancestors but raises ParseError if it hits a genuine minute-level (dt/nt) subtree it cannot coerce.
facts.refs: parser.py:74-108 (_Parser.__init__, parse(), uses_minute_operators), 227-264 (apply/coerce/daily_of), 284-293 (parse/parse_legacy entry points); test_general_call.py:69-77 (test_daily_coercion_for_nd_operators)

facts.topic: Q3 which operator families can consume a (D,S)-no-minute-axis leaf unchanged
facts.detail: If the new leaf's _infer_shape() returns exactly COLLAPSED (collapsed=True, degenerate=True, width=1 -- reusing the SAME Shape already used for a day_* output, not a new 4th kind), then operand_ok admits it with ZERO code changes for: cs_*/ts_* (nd face, needs_daily branch only checks sh.degenerate); cross_* (dt/cross family is NOT in the ('in','day') tuple that defines needs_full_m, so cross_* operators impose no shape restriction at all -- confirmed by test_shape_typing's cross_mean(day_mean(Close),5)->COLLAPSED,root=True); every elementwise/'shared' op (final fallback `return True`); and in_expand specifically (restores_m: sh.collapsed is satisfied even under strict). day_*/in_* (dt, family in ('in','day')) and nt_* (face=='nt') REJECT it under strict (needs_full_m requires genuine per-minute variation); under non-strict/legacy they reject it too for in_*/nt_* but would ACCEPT it for day_* specifically (the existing 'day_* over width-1' carve-out, originally meant for literal in_slice(...,w=1) subtrees) -- whether that carve-out should also silently accept the new leaf is a real design choice, not something the current code decides for a genuinely new leaf type.
facts.refs: expression.py:144-162 (operand_ok), axes.py:88-92,117-126 (needs_full_m / compute_axis_for -- cross excluded from the ('in','day') tuple), expression.py:186-196 (_output_shape), test_expression.py:8-21 (cross_mean(day_mean(Close),5) case)

facts.topic: Q3 current elementwise rule between a full-minute tensor and a day_*/degenerate one (static type level)
facts.detail: operand_ok imposes NO shape restriction on 'shared'-face (elementwise: add/sub/mul/div/eq/...) operators at all -- the final catch-all `return True` applies regardless of either operand's shape. So add(day_mean(Close), Close) IS a legal expression TODAY under the static type rules, with shape computed by _passthrough: given one COLLAPSED and one FULL operand, result.collapsed=False, result.degenerate=False, i.e. the combined shape collapses to FULL-equivalent. This is directly confirmed by the existing test suite, which already relies on day_*-vs-raw-minute-Feature mixing being legal: sub(Close, in_expand(day_mean(Close), 241)) parses to shape FULL (not a root).
facts.refs: expression.py:144-162 (operand_ok final `return True`), 175-183 (_passthrough), test_expression.py:14 (`sub(Close, in_expand(day_mean(Close), 241))` -> FULL)

facts.topic: Q3 same rule at the RUNTIME/engine level (outside the 3 assigned files, read for grounding)
facts.detail: At execution time the legality above is realised two different ways depending on operator family: for non-elementwise M-axis/D-axis ops (in_*, day_*, cross_*), engine/kernels.py's _align_widths() EXPLICITLY broadcasts any width-1 (day-collapsed/constant) operand up to the common minute width via `.expand(...).contiguous()` before the kernel runs (two genuinely different widths both >1 raises a ValueError there). For a node whose OWN family=='elementwise', apply_cube() skips _align_widths/_pre_collapse entirely (kernels.py:193-194) and calls the raw torch op directly -- it relies purely on PyTorch's native trailing-dimension broadcasting of the materialized (A,B,1) tensor against (A,B,M). A COLLAPSED node is kept with a literal trailing axis of size 1 inside a round (never squeezed to bare (A,B)); only at a ROUND BOUNDARY (schedule.py) does ANY degenerate node -- COLLAPSED or WIDE_DEGENERATE alike, the check is purely `n.shape.degenerate`, not `.collapsed` -- get handed off as a bare 2-D (S,D) panel (schedule.py:142-150). Consequence for the new leaf: if its raw stored form is read in as bare (A,B) (no trailing axis at all), it will NOT broadcast correctly against an (A,B,M) cube tensor under native torch rules (trailing dims would compare B against M); it must be materialised as (A,B,1) wherever it enters a cube-mode round, exactly mirroring how a day_* output already behaves -- this reshape point lives in whatever code reads leaves into a chunk, which is in engine.py/store.py, outside the 3 files I was assigned and NOT verified by me (see open_questions).
facts.refs: engine/kernels.py:73-77 (_expand_like), 122-143 (_align_widths), 186-229 (apply_cube, elementwise short-circuit at 193-194), 232-240 (apply_panel); engine/schedule.py:57-64 (_p_eligible), 138-150 (panel-hand-off keyed on `.shape.degenerate` only)

facts.topic: Q3 daily.py is NOT the mechanism needed

facts.topic: Q4 OpSpec fields
facts.detail: OpSpec (frozen dataclass) stores: name, face, family, category, arity, requires_window, fn, kernel_id, compute_axis, reduces_m, restores_m, lookahead, boolean_output, trivial_boolean, resource_risk, coarse_output, windows. Derived properties (not stored): needs_full_m, needs_daily, allowed_modes, non_root(=boolean_output or coarse_output).

facts.topic: Q4 _validate's own smoke test (accept/skip, NOT the boolean probe)
facts.detail: _validate(name, meta) decides only whether an operator is ACCEPTED into the registry at all (else recorded as a SkipRecord with a reason) by confirming its real output shape matches its declared category. For in_expand (RESTORES_M_NAMES): calls fn(x,3) on x=_sample(rows=7,cols=1,seed=1) (uniform [0.5,1.5), via torch.rand()+0.5) and requires output shape exactly (7,3). For everything else: classify(meta) maps (arity, requires_window, pair) to one of unary/binary/rolling/pair_rolling (returns None, i.e. reject, if no combination matches); _smoke_call feeds _sample(seed=1) (rows=7,cols=5) and, for binary/pair_rolling, a second _sample(seed=2); a 'day'-family kernel must collapse its last dim to size 1, every other kernel's output shape must equal its input's shape exactly, else rejected.
facts.refs: catalog.py:75-131 (classify, _sample, _smoke_call, _validate)

facts.topic: Q4 the 3 empirical cardinality/cost probes feeding OpSpec flags
facts.detail: boolean_output/coarse_output come from _probe_distinct_values: torch.Generator().manual_seed(7), x=randn(40,9) then y=randn(40,9) drawn SEQUENTIALLY off the same generator (not independently reseeded); if restores_m, x is sliced to its first column; dispatch by grammar category (unary/binary/rolling/else=pair_rolling) calls the kernel once and counts DISTINCT FINITE values after flattening -- boolean_output=(distinct<=2), coarse_output=(2<distinct<=3). trivial_boolean = boolean_output AND _probe_constant_capable: manual_seed(11), base=rand(40,9)+0.5 (strictly positive [0.5,1.5)), other=another draw off the same generator, tried over 4 input families in order -- (base,other), (-base,-other), (base,base), (randn,randn) off the continuing generator -- returning True on the FIRST family where the finite output collapses to <=1 distinct value (or is entirely non-finite/empty after filtering). resource_risk = name in SEARCH_FORBIDDEN_KERNELS({nt_ts_pearson,nt_ts_spearman,in_multireg}) OR name in POSITIONALLY_UNSAFE_KERNELS({pow}) OR (face!='nd' AND _probe_per_element_python(...)); the 3rd disjunct short-circuits (the expensive line-counting probe never runs for a name already caught by the first two, nor for any nd-face kernel). _probe_per_element_python (manual_seed(5), rand()+0.5) counts Python bytecode LINE events (via sys.settrace, deterministic/machine-independent) executed inside alphacube.operators at shapes (16,48) vs (64,48) vs (16,192); flags resource_risk if either larger run executes more than 2x+20 the baseline's lines (a vectorised kernel runs the same line count regardless of size; a Python-looping one scales).
facts.refs: catalog.py:183-220 (_probe_constant_capable), 223-275 (_probe_per_element_python), 278-296 (_probe_distinct_values), 378-402 (_make_spec wiring all 3 into OpSpec)

facts.topic: Q4 a separate, differently-scoped constant with a similar name
facts.detail: RESOURCE_RISK_KERNELS = frozenset({'ts_pearson','nt_ts_pearson','nt_ts_spearman','in_multireg'}) (catalog.py:56) is NOT the same thing as the OpSpec.resource_risk FIELD computed by _make_spec: it is a hand-picked, separately-exported constant (re-exported as DEFERRED_RESOURCE_OPERATORS by calculate.py) used by calculate.py / mining/gp.py / scripts/eval_legacy_factors.py to decide what to defer computationally for MEMORY reasons; it deliberately INCLUDES ts_pearson (the ND-face kernel), which the registry's own OpSpec.resource_risk correctly keeps OUT of SEARCH_FORBIDDEN_KERNELS (ts_pearson is ND-face, O(1942x cheaper) than its NT twin) -- this split is intentional and documented in catalog.py's own module docstring, not a bug, but the near-identical naming is a real foot-gun worth knowing before touching either.

facts.topic: Q4 why in_sustain_stddev is mis-flagged boolean_output -- verified by direct execution
facts.detail: in_sustain_stddev(mask, data, d, start_offset=0, num=False) (dt_in.py:832-843) is a pair_rolling op whose FIRST operand is semantically a {0,1} trigger mask (`torch.where(mask==1)` locates trigger cells); but every build-time probe (_probe_distinct_values's randn(40,9); all 4 of _probe_constant_capable's families, including (base,other) in [0.5,1.5)) feeds it CONTINUOUS random floats, which (for a continuous distribution) essentially never equal exactly 1.0. I re-ran both probes directly: on the exact probe input (manual_seed(7), randn(40,9) x2), `(x==1).sum()`==0, so `_get_rowwise_windows` finds zero trigger rows and the function returns an all-NaN (40,9) tensor every time (fill_value=NaN since num defaults False) -> 0 distinct finite values (<=2) -> boolean_output=True; the same all-NaN/empty-after-filter outcome on every one of _probe_constant_capable's 4 families -> trivial_boolean=True too. in_sustain_stddev is one of AlphaCube's OWN built-in kernels (not in Partura's ops_ext.py NEW_OPERATORS list), so Partura's current blanket flag-clearing (which only iterates NEW_OPERATORS) does NOT fix it -- it stays mis-flagged even with partura.ops_ext loaded.
facts.refs: operators/dt_in.py:819-843 (in_sustain_mean/in_sustain_stddev, _get_rowwise_windows at ~800); verified live via /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/design/probe_boolean_flags.py run on 2026-10-05: 'distinct finite output values on the probe panel: 0', 'trivial-capable: True', 'num exact mask==1 cells in x: 0'

facts.topic: Q4 the '9 ratio-class operators' claim -- verified empirically, not assumed
facts.detail: I rebuilt the registry using the ORIGINAL (unpatched) catalog.build_registry function object (saved before importing partura.ops_ext, so Partura's flag-clearing monkeypatch never ran) but with ops_ext's 45 @op(...)-decorated functions already merged into the shared OPERATOR_REGISTRY dict (which happens merely by importing the module, independent of its install() call). Exactly 9 base operator names come back boolean_output=True AND trivial_boolean=True (coarse_output=False in every case): day_flat_ratio, day_zero_ratio, day_flat_run_max, day_at_max_ratio, day_at_min_ratio, day_distinct_ratio (all dt/day family), cross_flat_ratio (dt/cross), cs_bucket_demean, cs_bucket_zscore (nd/cs, each with an nt_ twin ALSO flagged, since the cardinality probe is face-independent and runs once per registration -> 11 total flagged registry entries, 9 unique base names). Two distinct failure mechanisms: (A) the 7 day_*/cross_* ones all test EXACT EQUALITY (x==prev, x==max, distinct-value counting) against continuous torch.randn data, where ties essentially never occur, so the ratio collapses to one constant (usually exactly 0.0, or 1/9, or 1.0) across all 40 probe rows; (B) cs_bucket_demean/cs_bucket_zscore decile-bucket into 10 buckets but the probe's cross-sectional axis has only N=9 columns, so every bucket ends up with exactly 0 or 1 members and the kernels' own `n>=2` validity gate is NEVER satisfied -> output is ALL-NaN (not just constant; 0 finite values) on the probe panel.

facts.topic: Q4 how 'declare real-valued' is currently faked, and why it's safe to make it a first-class hook
facts.detail: Partura's ops_ext.install() (ops_ext.py:729-759) does NOT touch the probes; it runs the normal (misflagging) build, then post-hoc overwrites the OpSpec via `dataclasses.replace(sp, boolean_output=False, trivial_boolean=False)` for every name in NEW_OPERATORS (+nt twins) found flagged -- leaves coarse_output untouched, is keyed by an externally-maintained hardcoded name list, and is applied via monkeypatching the catalog.build_registry function object itself (guarded by a `build_registry._partura` sentinel so it only wraps once). A first-class alternative: add a boolean kwarg to operators/common.py's op() decorator (op(...), stored into the OPERATOR_REGISTRY[name] meta dict) that catalog.py's _make_spec reads and, when True, SKIPS calling _probe_distinct_values/_probe_constant_capable entirely (forcing boolean_output=trivial_boolean=coarse_output=False) instead of overriding their result. This is safe for the 'byte-identical when no new argument is passed' constraint for two independent reasons: (1) every existing @op(...) call site keeps the new kwarg at its default (False/off), so no existing OpSpec changes; (2) each probe already constructs its OWN fresh, locally-seeded torch.Generator() (manual_seed(7) / manual_seed(11) / manual_seed(5)) rather than touching any shared/global RNG stream, so skipping the probe call for a declared-real kernel cannot perturb any OTHER kernel's probe outcome or the random stream the search grammar itself draws from.
facts.refs: ops_ext.py:729-759 (install()); operators/common.py:56-71 (op() decorator + OPERATOR_REGISTRY dict shape); catalog.py:378-402 (_make_spec, where the new kwarg would short-circuit); catalog.py:88-90,196-197,280-281 (each probe's self-contained torch.Generator())

insertion_points.change: Add a second leaf class with its own `field` slot and an `_infer_shape()` that returns COLLAPSED (collapsed=True, degenerate=True, width=1) instead of FULL, so every existing shape rule (operand_ok, _passthrough, _output_shape) treats it exactly like an existing day_* output with zero changes to those functions. Give it its own key() tag (e.g. 'DF:{field}', not 'F:{field}') so it can never collide with a same-named minute Feature in the key()-based CSE/dedup/ban machinery used throughout mining/* and engine/dag.py.

result.summary: Read-only fact map for AlphaCube's expression/parser/catalog type system (files: src/alphacube/expression.py, parser.py, catalog.py, axes.py, operators/common.py, plus fullcatalog.py, daily.py, tradability.py, engine/kernels.py, engine/schedule.py, scripts/tearsheet.py, synthetic.py and the relevant tests/*.py, all read for grounding -- only expression.py/parser.py/catalog.py/operators-common were the assigned targets). No files were modified; one throwaway introspection script was written to /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/design/probe_boolean_flags.py and run read-only via PYTHONPATH=/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src ~/.venvs/alphacube/bin/python to empirically verify (not guess) which operators the catalog's boolean/trivial-boolean probes mis-flag.\n\nHeadline findings: (1) Expression's type system is 2 leaf kinds (Feature/Constant) + 4 operator-node kinds (Unary/Binary/Rolling/PairRolling, all built through the single make_node/_OpNode.__init__ check) + GeneralCall (a second, separate check, used only by the parser for research/legacy expressions). Shape is just 2 booleans (collapsed, degenerate) + optional width -- 'daily' is a property ALIAS of degenerate, not an independent axis; 3 named constants (FULL/COLLAPSED/WIDE_DEGENERATE) cover what's actually built. (2) is_valid_root is a narrow 3-condition root-only check; the real defense against a 'boolean laundered through arithmetic' root is Registry.searchable()'s vocabulary filter, a different mechanism entirely -- important for designing the 'declare real-valued' hook, since fixing the OpSpec flag at registration time satisfies both mechanisms at once. (3) A new (D,S)-no-minute-axis daily leaf, if given shape=COLLAPSED (reusing exactly the Shape a day_* output already uses), is accepted with ZERO code changes by cs_*/ts_*, cross_*, all elementwise ops, and in_expand; it is rejected by day_*/in_*/nt_* under strict (and by in_*/nt_* under legacy too) -- all verified from the actual operand_ok/axes.py logic, cross-checked against engine/kernels.py+schedule.py to confirm how a day_*-vs-raw-Feature elementwise mix is materialised today (COLLAPSED kept as a real (A,B,1) trailing axis in-round; only degenerate-ness, not collapsed-ness, decides the (S,D)-bare-panel round-boundary hand-off). (4) I ran catalog.py's ORIGINAL (unpatched) build_registry against Partura's 45 new operators and confirmed empirically -- not assumed -- that exactly 9 base names (day_flat_ratio, day_zero_ratio, day_flat_run_max, day_at_max_ratio, day_at_min_ratio, day_distinct_ratio, cross_flat_ratio, cs_bucket_demean, cs_bucket_zscore) get boolean_output=trivial_boolean=True from 2 distinct causes (exact-equality tests that never fire on continuous random floats; a decile-bucket `n>=2` validity gate that never fires with only 9 probe columns), and separately confirmed exactly why AlphaCube's own in_sustain_stddev is mis-flagged (its mask operand never equals 1.0 under continuous random probe data, so it always returns all-NaN). (5) None of the existing tests pin down an exact boolean/trivial-flagged operator set, so today's mis-flags are silent -- a new test asserting the full set (or at least the known-good/known-bad lists) would catch regressions.
